EGLL-KJFK: London Heathrow and New York JFK form the busiest long haul international route, and the only one in the top ten that crosses an ocean.
Supersonic Concorde once covered it in about three and a half hours before retiring in 2003.
EGLL-KLAX: This route links the United Kingdom's biggest airport with the heart of the American entertainment industry.
EGLL-OMDB: This route connects Europe with Dubai, one of the world's great transfer hubs between Europe, Asia and Africa.
OMDB-YSSY: It is one of the key links between the Gulf and Australia, crossing the Indian Ocean on a very long flight.
EGLL-WSSS: It is a classic leg of the Kangaroo Route, the historic air link between Britain and Australia.
WSSS-YSSY: It links two of the busiest gateways in Asia Pacific, and Singapore is a major transfer point for Australia.
KLAX-YSSY: This trans Pacific route crosses the International Date Line, so the calendar date jumps during the flight.
KLAX-RJTT: This trans Pacific route links two giant Pacific coast economies, Southern California and Japan.
KJFK-RJTT: It connects two of the largest metropolitan areas on Earth, New York and Tokyo.
KJFK-OTHH: It links New York with Qatar's Gulf hub on a long flight across the Atlantic and Europe.
EGLL-OTHH: It links London with Doha, a major hub connecting Europe to Asia, Africa and Australia.
EGLL-VHHH: It is a classic Europe to Asia route, linking London with one of the world's great financial centers.
KJFK-LFPG: It links two of the world's most visited cities across the North Atlantic.
EDDF-KJFK: It connects Frankfurt, a major European financial center, with New York across the North Atlantic.
EDDF-KORD: It links Frankfurt with Chicago, one of the biggest hubs in the United States.
KJFK-OMAA: Abu Dhabi offers United States border preclearance, so travelers heading to America clear immigration before they fly.
KLAX-RKSI: It links Seoul with Los Angeles, home to one of the largest Korean communities outside Korea.
KSFO-RJTT: It links Silicon Valley's gateway with the heart of Tokyo across the North Pacific.
KJFK-LTFM: It links New York with Istanbul, a city that sits on two continents.
EGLL-LTFM: It links London with Istanbul, a city that sits on both Europe and Asia.
EHAM-KJFK: Amsterdam is home to KLM, founded in 1919 and the oldest airline still flying under its original name.
EHAM-KLAX: It links Amsterdam with Los Angeles, a long transatlantic and continental flight on the KLM network.
EGLL-VIDP: It links London with Delhi, one of the busiest air corridors between Europe and South Asia.
EGLL-FACT: It links London with Cape Town, one of the longest running air links between Britain and southern Africa.

EGLL-YPPH: Qantas links London and Perth non-stop, connecting Britain with the west coast of Australia.
KDFW-YMML: Qantas connects Texas with Melbourne non-stop, one of the longest routes in the world.

WMKK-WSSS: Malaysia and Singapore are close neighbors, and this short hop ranks among the busiest international routes anywhere.
